# Blaise 1.10.3: Google Meet participants again
Your meetings, transcripts, notes and settings carry over untouched, and nothing needs reprocessing.
## Fixed
- **Google Meet participants, speaker names and auto-end.** Google is moving call tabs to a new address (`meet.google.com/meet/<code>`). The Meet extension read that address as a meeting called "meet", so Blaise could not connect the call to its recording: no participants, no automatic end, and a "no signals" reminder on every Meet call. The extension and the app now read the meeting code from both address forms. - **Launch & Record** opens the Meet link that carries the meeting it records, even when an invite contains more than one Meet link.
## Update the Meet extension (one manual step)
The app updates itself; the Chrome extension does not. To get the fix:
1. Download `blaise-meet-extension.zip` below and unzip it over the folder you loaded the extension from (or load the new folder). 2. In `chrome://extensions`, press **Reload** on "Blaise Meet Companion". It should read version **0.3.1**. 3. Refresh any open Google Meet tab.
Your shared secret survives the reload; you don't need to enter it again.
## Assets
- `Blaise-1.10.3.zip`: the notarised, stapled app (macOS 15.6.1+, Apple Silicon) - `blaise-meet-extension.zip`: the Chrome extension for Google Meet participant/speaker signals (0.3.1, updated)

# Blaise 1.10.2: current Claude models, and a separate model for the memory digest
Your meetings, transcripts, notes and settings carry over untouched, and nothing needs reprocessing.
## What's new
- **More Claude models for notes.** Settings → Engines → Notes now offers Sonnet 5.5, Opus 5.5 and Haiku 4.5 through the API, beside Sonnet 4.6, and Opus 5.5 beside Sonnet 5.5 on the Claude subscription. Your saved choice and credentials carry over, and API spend is priced at the chosen model's rates. Sonnet 5.5 and Opus 5.5 think before writing, on both the API and the subscription. Contributed by Arthur Soares (@arthursoares), #17. - **A separate model for the memory digest.** Settings → Engines → Memory digest. It defaults to "Same as notes"; pick another model and only the digest uses it. If that model can't run, the digest waits and retries on its own, and your notes are not affected. For a fully offline setup, keep the digest on "Same as notes" or on the local engine too.
## Changed
- The default engines are renamed in the picker: "Claude Sonnet 4.6 (API)" and "Claude Sonnet 5.5 (subscription)". - An AI edit whose API call fails no longer falls back to the Claude subscription; it waits for the engine you chose.
## Fixed
- **Long digests.** The API digest has room for a long meeting, and a digest that still runs out is retried later instead of being saved cut off. - **Recording.** Pressing start or resume twice no longer crashes; a failed pause no longer blocks the next recording; the timer keeps counting after a resume; the quit dialog says processing happens at the next launch. - **Notes.** AI Correct and Add Note aimed at a whole table land under that table; the selection bar stays inside a narrow notes pane; the notes engine reports its real error on its last attempt. - **Calendar.** A calendar added or removed shows up in an open Settings picker. - **Upgrading from 1.10.1:** delivered in place by the updater.
## Assets
- `Blaise-1.10.2.zip`: the notarised, stapled app (macOS 15.6.1+, Apple Silicon) - `blaise-meet-extension.zip`: the Chrome extension for Google Meet participant/speaker signals (unchanged)

# Blaise 1.10.1: your voice stays in playback after the Mac sleeps
A fix release. Your meetings, transcripts, notes and settings carry over untouched, and nothing needs reprocessing.
## What changed
- **Playback after a sleep.** If the Mac went to sleep during a recording (closing the lid, for example), playback could drop your own microphone track, and the timecode marks on the things you said disappeared from the notes. Nothing was lost: both tracks were always on disk. Blaise now plays both, so your voice and those timecodes come back, including on meetings recorded before this version. - **Reprocess All shows the real cost.** The confirmation used to price every meeting at the metered API rate, even with the Claude subscription engine or a local engine selected, and could cap how many meetings it queued because of that. It now uses the cost of the engine you selected. - **Google Calendar sign-in.** The sign-in page escapes any error text it shows, and an interrupted sign-in releases its temporary local port straight away. - **For contributors:** the sharded test runner stops when the test build fails instead of reporting the previous build's results, and the test scripts run in a fixed time zone so date tests pass anywhere. - **Upgrading from 1.10.0:** delivered in place by the updater.
## Assets
- `Blaise-1.10.1.zip`: the notarised, stapled app (macOS 15.6.1+, Apple Silicon) - `blaise-meet-extension.zip`: the Chrome extension for Google Meet participant/speaker signals (unchanged)
